pieces.label: Board — the playing floor
pieces.blurb: 8×8 of worn stone set flush with the floor. Mortar, grit, dust drifts, and impact scarring.
pieces.biggestGap: Light squares need bold dark branching ink-veins and a broad dust-scuffed polish; the reflection is mirror-sharp and the inlaid border strip is missing.

history.gap: no marble veining; floor is the lowest-detail region when in the film it is the highest

pieces.critiqueDetail: gradientAnisotropy 1.95 vs the film 2.68 — gradients are blobby because there is no veining, joint inlay or directional grain. Round-2 builder did not run (spend limit).

pieces.label: Pieces — carved stone chessmen
pieces.blurb: Six piece types per side as chiselled, weathered, chipped stone. Judged at extreme low angle.
pieces.biggestGap: Round-2 rebuild landed figurative geometry; not yet re-critiqued (spend limit).

history.gap: no figurative geometry — cones, not carved combatants

pieces.critiqueDetail: Round 1 was judged obviously a render: no figurative geometry, and detailTotal HIGHER than the film (0.0233 vs 0.0135) proving the energy was faceting noise rather than carving. Round 2 rebuilt with explicit limbs, mouldings and colonnettes plus crease-angle shading.

pieces.label: Destruction — stone breaking stone
pieces.blurb: Angular fracture, bright fresh interior faces, debris that settles, dust lit through.

pieces.label: Camera — lens and operator
pieces.blurb: Anamorphic character, real depth of field, handheld weight, reaction lag on impacts, film grain.

pieces.label: Chess — rules and engine
pieces.blurb: Full legal chess verified by perft, plus a search that genuinely fights back. Judged on numbers, not looks.
pieces.biggestGap: none — perft exact on all five standard positions

history.gap: none — all perft values exact, engine wins 40/40 sparring games

pieces.critiqueDetail: Perft matches published node counts exactly at every depth tested. Search ~542k nodes/sec, finds mate-in-1 and mate-in-2 and scores them as forced mates, returns null on a mated position. Sparring 20-0 vs random mover and 20-0 vs greedy material mover.

pieces.label: Game — the fight itself
pieces.blurb: Turn loop, pieces walking, captures triggering destruction, the engine answering, checkmate ending it.
pieces.biggestGap: none on function — all three demo lines independently verified as real checkmates

history.gap: none — 3/3 demo lines verified as real checkmate with zero legal replies

pieces.critiqueDetail: Turn loop drives the verified engine. Captures trigger strike, shatter, light flare, camera shake and marble scarring; wreckage stays on the board for the rest of the game. Checkmate ends it with the king releasing its blade. Interactive click-to-move works against the engine. Replay is a pure function of world.time so captures stay deterministic.
